utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before we begin, I'd like to apologise to all of the people here concerned. I was stuck in traffic due to road construction. I was late a little bit. I'm sorry about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. We have Witness C-047 to conclude. According to my note, Mr. Milosevic, you have an hour and a quarter cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. C-047, you showed us a certificate testifying to the fact that you were in the 4th Lika Brigade in the autumn and winter of 1991 to 1992; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I was not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And where -- how come we have this certificate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The volunteers who were there brought me that certificate and I stated straight away that I was not actually there myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not saying what you said. This is what it says on the certificate.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That is indeed what it says on the certificate but I was not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that this is a forgery, a forged certificate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The certificate is original, but what I'm saying is that I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't understand this. You say that the certificate is the original one, but the fact that your name is written there, that is not correct; is that it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not there. It does say so in the paper, in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, how come you weren't there and yet you're given orders and travel instructions to travel to Belgrade at the time you were not there, travel from the unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in Petrinje, in the -- I was not in the 4th Lika Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You didn't travel to Belgrade? So as you weren't there, you couldn't have travelled from -- to Belgrade from the unit --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you I was not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And what about these certificates giving you travel authorisation from Belgrade from the 4th Lika Brigade? Is that something that has been invented, fabricated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I think the witness should be given those certificate, because there are three different certificates and there may be a confusion now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Which numbers, please? Which tab numbers.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The first tab number, that's the one from the Lika Brigade. That's number 12. And the other are number 13 and number 14.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Let the witness have the documents.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you mean this 4th Lika one?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And it says that you were there from 1991 to 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says here. That's what is written. But I wasn't there. They sent me the certificate because I was the commander of the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And what about these travel authorisations? Did they send you that too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an order for Petrinje. I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just take a look at the date. One was there on the 18th of March, 1994, and the other was the 5th of October, 1993, when the unit went to Petrinje, or rather --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. The certificate that relates to 1991 and 1992, that is the period of time when the JNA was in the area while Yugoslavia still existed; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the JNA was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Because this is the beginning of 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the JNA did exist then.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And it was a unit within the composition of the JNA; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you don't know any specific details about that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milan Stojanovic was at the head of this particular unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. When you were asked during the examination-in-chief with respect to the records, you said that the records were kept by the Territorial Defence and the JNA, depending on which formation one belonged to; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And is it also right, what the Serbian Radical Party claims, that they recruited volunteers exclusively for the JNA and the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I said is it true and correct what is otherwise claimed by the Serbian Radical Party, and that is that it recruited volunteers exclusively for the JNA and the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serbian Radical Party had its Chetnik Movement, and those units, when they went into the field, either belonged to the TO or the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean then that the volunteers were recruited for the JNA and the TO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the Serbian Chetnik Movement and could not work independently and autonomously on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In tab 16 -- let's just clear this up a minute. In tab 16, you have an order which states towards the ends of the first paragraph, "Within the composition of the Territorial Defence." That's what it says here. Which means they were recruited to help make up the complement of the Territorial Defence. And Western Slavonia is mentioned here, the composition of the Territorial Defence; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that the Serbian Radical Party did have a Serbian Chetnik Movement which was organised as a military formation, which was either armed in Serbia, in Voj Potok [phoen], or elsewhere, when it went to the TO, to the place it was being assigned to, or to the JNA command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, if you can deal with tab -- this document, tab 16, which speaks of all volunteers sent to Western Slavonia be put under the command of a name as members of the Territorial Defence. What -- how do you interpret that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That means every unit from Serbia, the Serbian Chetnik Movement, when it goes into the field, has to report to the TO or to JNA headquarters and command. And it says here that the commander was Noncic Radovan. He was a member of the Serbian Radical Party, the Serbian Chetnik Movement, and that he was going with the unit within the composition of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: No Chetnik Movement is mentioned here, only the Serbian Radical Party is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serbian Chetnik Movement was not registered.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Was it a secret organisation, then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a public organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And yet it wasn't registered?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't registered, Mr. Milosevic. But they were issued weapons from the JNA, equipment, materiel, food was supplied, transport, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you want to say that when you were a JNA reservist you were armed like the rest of the reservists of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But as Chetniks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, that is very difficult to believe. Do you have evidence and proof of this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, you haven't presented any evidence to that effect here.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I did mention an example in Bajina Basta where we were issued weapons, and a complete military set of equipment --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: As for Bajina Basta, what I understood was that they disarmed you and let you go.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not right. That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, these are facts that you spoke about yourself except that you're saying that you went of your own free will.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true, and you can check it out. You can check out the reason for which I left the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, how do you explain the second sentence in that same order which says, "volunteers who leave the unit of their own accord will be treated as fugitives of the Serbian Radical Party and the Serbian Radical Party will not protect them in any way"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume that applies to individual, but I don't know of than example of that happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Does that imply that certain individuals perform certain crimes and they were sort of renegades, fugitives from the regular units to which they had applied as volunteers and the Serbian Radical Party emphasises by this that it won't protect them because it does not consider that -- that to be lawful -- a lawful act? Is that right or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know that anybody was sent away from the battlefield of the Serbian -- by the Serbian Radical Party.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, the fact that you don't know about it, does that mean that nobody was let go because he behaved -- they behaved in an undisciplined manner or committed an offence of any kind or was arrested for committing an offence of some kind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. In tab 9, it was said that fighters returning, that for lack of discipline special records were kept of those offences. So from those aspects, when you look at all those facts and data, as far as I can see, insistence was made upon the fact that the volunteers in the units in which they were registered had to behave properly in keeping with military rules and regulations. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's how it should have been in units and the command of those units.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now, tell me this, please: You mentioned a crime perpetrated by those volunteers of yours, and you also said that they killed three Croats. I'm sure you'll remember that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My volunteers did not commit a single crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: No, they did not, did they? Well, whose volunteers were they, then, these men who perpetrated the crime that you're talking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you talk about Vukovar? Is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, we didn't get the question. Would you repeat the question, please, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned the fact that these volunteers - that's what you said - killed three Croats. That's what you said during your main testimony. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which volunteers, Mr. Milosevic, and where?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Those members of yours.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Who then?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Can you refer, a bit more precisely, to the incident which you want the witness to deal with.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, I have made a note of that here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. When --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wrote down --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let's try and find it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- What the witness was saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Were you witness to any crime - let me turn the question round and put it this way - did you witness any crime that was committed, any crime at all? Did you witness a crime at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw the one in Tordinci and I did in Vukovar too, the premises where they were killed. That's what I said. The Chetniks of Milan Lancuzanin in a --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What did you see there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They said they had killed these three Croats and they took me to a room, a bathroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: They told you they had killed these three Croats?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And then I was there when a young girl was brought in, and they said in front of everybody that they would kill her, rape her, and she never returned in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now, tell me this: In view of the position you occupied, were these individuals people whom you knew?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw them for the first time then.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Were they men from your party?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serbian Radical Party.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You were able to identify them; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could now. I couldn't at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, in view of the job you did --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: -- Did you -- as to what you claim happened, did you table a report, write a report to anybody?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spoke to Jerinkic and told him what had happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking you whether you talked about it to anybody, but did you file a report?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not a written report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, do you know that you are duty-bound to compile a report even when a travel accident occurs? And we're dealing with a killing here.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I say, it was a killing on the battlefield in Croatia, and I reported this orally.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So may we take it and note that you did not table a report to anybody that a killing had taken place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told Milan Jerinkic orally about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What did you say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told him orally.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I see, orally. So you didn't file a report of any kind.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not a written report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now, tell me, who's Mirko Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mirko Blagojevic is a Chetnik commander. I think he's a Vojvoda.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You think?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sure he's a Vojvoda.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Was he from Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He should be. I think he is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, you showed us a statement here by him dated September 1992. "In Northern Bosnia between the 24th to 25th of September where he is protesting against a unit of some kind which seems to have committed a killing, the killing of some Muslims. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I be allowed to see the document, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Tab 11.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I've seen this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So does that mean that he protected Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that in Bijeljina and in that area in general there were even units of the Army of Republika Srpska in which there was a large number of Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I was not aware of him having protected Muslims. He disassociated himself from the crime that had been committed by the police, according to this document, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Does that mean that they considered the killing of those Muslims a crime?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, because they had not committed it. It was committed by the police of the MUP of Republika Srpska, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that it was precisely them who tried to protect all the Muslims in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You don't know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know what Arkan did, but I'm not aware of this protection.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. You mentioned Vocin. Were you in Vocin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but I did hear about the crime that was committed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And who was it that committed this crime?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, members of the Serb Chetnik Movement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Oh, so they were the members of your movement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not of my movement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But you said that you joined that movement in order to topple Milosevic and the Communists. That that's what you said by way of an explanation in your statement.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So now, if you say that it was not your movement, make up your mind. Is it your movement or is it not your movement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware of that unit. My unit did completely different things, and it was supposed to have completely different objectives. However, you know that in Serbia there were a great many Chetnik units.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I assume, since you rallied together to topple me, as you had put it, that you should know this better than me. So do you know, who did this? Did you identify these persons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I just know that they are Chetniks from Serbia, not from Vojvodina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you cannot identify these men but you know that they are members of this same movement that you belonged to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, since I cannot link all of this up somehow, what was your role then? You were a member of the Serbian Chetnik Movement, you say. Then you say here that they committed crimes. But at the same time, you say that you have nothing to do with that. Now, tell me, who does have something to do with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have anything to do with these crimes and I don't know whose -- under whose command they were, who their commander was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What was your role? Did you have a unit of the Serb Chetnik Movement under your command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from my territory, if I can put it that way. From the area where I lived.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. What was your role?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We also went to the frontline, but we did not commit crimes. We did not loot, nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So your unit did not commit crimes and these other units did commit crimes; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not saying that all units did. I'm saying that individual units did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did you see a single one of these crimes that was committed by any one of these units that you've referred to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I saw this in Vukovar, in Tordinci, I saw what happened there, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So in two places. You personally saw a crime in two places.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that way, yes. But as for killings during the war, I saw that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw this after the Chetniks would go by.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Oh, so you would see it afterwards. Did you personally see a killing being committed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did, in Njemci. But the man was already dead after I arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you did not see the actual killing -- the man had already been dead?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They talked about it themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you heard about this from the persons who were talking about it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there and I saw the corpse, the body of this man, if I can put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did you submit a report about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Why didn't you submit a report?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was the war operation zone and the police from my area could not do anything there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It can provide information; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Information to who, Mr. Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: To the police.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Other police in Serbia. If you assumed that this was done by someone from Serbia, then it is logical that you should provide this information to the police in Serbia. That is anybody's civic duty, regardless of whether he or she is organised in a movement or not, like a movement that you just referred to.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not aware of any such information having existed.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Repeat the question, if you would.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I asked, Mr. May, whether he reported to anyone on this what he had heard. And we established that he had heard it. But did he submit a report in writing? That was my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He's answered that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Tell me, since you said several times that you had long war experience, where did you acquire this experience?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was at quite a few of these positions, as they were called, Slavonia, Baranja, Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And now, describe this experience of yours to me, please, this long war experience that you had.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you want know describe?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What was your position? How did you acquire this experience? You say that you took part in the Territorial Defence or in the JNA; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And what did you do? Were you on the defence or did you go out to kill?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we were at positions, and at some places there were shooting and at some places there was only guarding of these positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Who were you guarding these positions from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we were at the separation line with the Croats or with the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You say on page 8 that the volunteers went through brief training in Subotica at the police training ground at Veliki Radinovac. This was at a state compound that was used by the SUP. According to the information that I have, this is incorrect.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: But it is correct. I was with them personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that there was no training going on whatsoever in Veliki Radinovac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean no training? What do you mean -- I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You were there yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there myself with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Who was there with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Volunteers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Since you say that this is a police training ground.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Were any of the police there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had agreed with Milan Jerinkic that I could go there for a while.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So there were no police there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there was no need for them to be there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And now you claim that you had agreed on this with Jerinkic, that you should go there; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Explain this to me, please: Let me just have a look. Let's see which tab this is. It looks like 21, tab 21. "Press conference, with weapons." Tab 21.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let the witness have a copy of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I am looking at this now. I'm looking at this facsimile of the newspapers. It says "Press conference under arms." And then there's also a headline saying "Timely action by the police," and it says that the press conference had barely ended, the press conference of the Serb Radical Party, when a statement arrived from the MUP that measures were taken to identify men in camouflage uniform and under arms. Such swift reaction is justified, because otherwise the public would certainly be disturbed because over the local radio a report had been broadcast from the press conference and immediately after that the statement of the MUP. On the basis of which one may conclude that the state organs are prepared in spite of the unstable situation in the country of the work they are in charge of." So you had a press conference here, and the MUP said that measures were taken immediately to identify those who had this. And there was swift reaction to what had been going on. So how can you say that in agreement with the police you went there to some kind of training ground where there is no police whatsoever but they told you that you could go there and train? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that is right. We were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You made all of this up.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not make it up. I was there myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, do you know that this is on the outskirts of Subotica? This is a suburb with family homes, and it's populated by Hungarians predominantly. About 90 per cent of the population is Hungarian.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, there is a training ground where we trained, and so did the special police forces. All of this is within Veliki Radinovac. I am very well aware of this terrain. A large amount of it is a forest.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I assume that you know, but I have information here that says there is barracks there with the regular army. So did you train near the barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, the barracks is on the E-5 road, on the main road. And this is a very big area, Veliki Radinovac. It's a large territory. There is a populated area and there is a forest there too. There is a vast forest.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You went into the forest?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: To train?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: There were no police there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But you did ask the police for permission to go and train there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because my unit, this special police unit, did train precisely in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Special police unit? You were talking about your group. You're now talking about a special police unit.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. The members of the Serb Chetnik Movement were being trained there too.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Are you talking about training of the special police unit or about your training?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm saying that it's one and the same area, one and the same training grounds.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What was that?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone. We're sorry. We can't hear anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just -- will you both -- will you both pause so that we can get this microphone switched on. Could you pause too, C-047? Now, I don't quite know the point of this questioning. The witness has said all along that it was members of his unit who were being trained and that the police gave him permission to do so. I think we've probably exhausted this matter. He's described where it was too. Yes, if you'd go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That you had approval of the police is something that you are just claiming orally. Your don't really have any proof.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, in appreciation of what Jerinkic did, Dusko Stipanovic and Radovan Knezevic - but then he returned this - in 1992 these men were giving thank-you certificates for good cooperation. This also had to do with the press conference that was held. So these thank-you certificates were issued in writing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you got thank-you certificates for this press conference that the MUP reacted to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not me. It was this head of MUP precisely who got this thank-you certificate from the Serb Chetnik Movement, whereas Radovan Knezevic refused to accept it and he returned it.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: On page 8, paragraph 7 you say that all Serbs at that time were sympathisers of the Serb Radical Party? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't mean it quite literally, but a large number at any rate.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. If you say that there was a large number of sympathisers at the Serb Radical Party, how many votes did the Serb Radical Party win in the elections, considering this large number of sympathisers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know anything about this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not really follow elections. I wasn't interested in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that these figures are in contrast to what you've been claiming all along?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there were a great many members of the Serb Radical Party, members of the Serb Chetnik Movement, and sympathisers, a great many.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That's why I asked you. How many votes did this mean for the Serb Radical Party in the elections when it had so many sympathisers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said, Mr. Milosevic, that I was not interested in politics. I am not interested in politics, especially not those elections.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Can you enumerate all the places where you fought at the frontline? According to what I received here, you haven't been anywhere, and you're making all this up.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did. And on the 27th of July, I was proclaimed a colonel.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters did not hear the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Vojvoda Abramovic and another Vojvoda were at the Adult Education University in March --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You got the rank of colonel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We're having problems with the microphone. I'm just going to ask the registrar about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Now, look, the problem is that you mustn't respond, Witness C-047, until you see his, the accused's, microphone off. Could you watch his microphone and it's only when it's off that you respond. You both speak the same language, and it's difficult for anyone to keep up if we don't keep these pauses. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Oh, you were very generous with all these ranks amongst yourselves. Tell me, on page 10, paragraph 4, you say that "Vojvoda Momcilo Djuic was the greatest donor you had and that he lived in Toronto and that he sent money from there." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, Vojvoda Seselj got a large amount of money from Djuic when he was proclaimed a Vojvoda.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I am asking you whether this is what you stated. "He was the greatest donor. He lived in Toronto, Canada, and he sent money there. "

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you know at all that Djuic did not live in Toronto, Canada. He lived in California, in the USA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly I made a mistake, but I know that he sent money.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What is it that you know and what is it that you made a mistake about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that when Vojvoda Seselj was proclaimed a Vojvoda, that Djuic gave him a large amount of money for the organisation of Serb Chetnik units for the struggle against communism. That was the objective.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you about the other thing. You claimed that he lived in Canada and that he sent money from there, from Toronto, and he never lived in Canada. He lived in America -- or rather, in the United States of America, in California at that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly I might have made a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is it possible that you might have made a mistake in terms of everything that you've been talking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not possible. I am giving arguments.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. All right. Let's change the subject, then, please. Do you know who collected humanitarian aid during the war for the war-ravaged areas, food, medical supplies, clothing, blankets, and these supplies were accompanied by appropriate documents, stamped documents from the Red Cross in Subotica and so on and so forth? Do you know who was involved in that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Red Cross, as far as I know, sent aid through the SPS, whereas the radicals collected aid in a different manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The certificate returned to those who were sending aid. Therefore, the Socialist Party of Serbia sent aid in food, medicine, clothing, blankets, et cetera, through the Red Cross of Subotica; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: On page 10, paragraph 3 you say that your financing went through the Radikal Komerc company; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: According to my information, this firm founded in 1992, Radikal Komerc was founded by some citizen and not by the party.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I see. It is not true. Is the following true that I have as information? It's quite possible that my information may be wrong. Just say yes or no. Do you know that this company functioned for less than two months and that on its account there is no input or output of a single dinar and that the director of the company was a certain Nebojsa Ilic who was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: One thing at a time. One thing at a time. What is alleged, Witness C-047, is that, first of all, the company functioned for less than two months. Would you agree with that or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For how long it lasted, I don't know. But I know who founded and when it was founded. And the offices were in the premises of the Serbian Radical Party.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: According to information checked by my associates, there was not a single dinar paid in or withdrawn from those -- from that account during those two months. It was a firm that somebody wanted to start operating but it never succeeded. So there's not a single dinar being paid in or withdrawn from their account. Do you know Nebojsa Ilic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know him. But you didn't mention Djordjija Lekic. He led that company. He was in charge.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: According to my information, the director was Nebojsa Ilic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly. But I know Djordjija Lekic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But this Nebojsa Ilic was quickly eliminated.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that. He completed his education and then he went back to Sabac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And you explain here the reason for your conflict. Tell me, please, who is Vujic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bozidar Vujic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You had a conflict with Vujic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I had some disagreements with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And who is this Vujic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean who? He's a man from Subotica, Bozidar Vujic. He worked in the 29th of November company in the warehouse. He was a founder of the Serbian Radical Party in Subotica. As far as I know, he is a member of parliament today.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: As he was a warehouse-keeper in the 29th of November Meat Processing Factory and he's the person who founded the Serbian Radical Party in Subotica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: From what it says on page 10, you had a dispute with him because you did not want to take part in killings of citizens and other crimes, but that it was customary for your volunteer units to kill and loot. Did Vujic ask you to kill and loot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not worded properly. I mention again the volunteer unit from Subotica did not kill or loot.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I asked you something else. Did Vujic asked you to kill and loot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He asked us to go into the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did he ask you to kill and loot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was normal. If you go there, that was logical. What would you do? What else would you do?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So it was logical for you when you go into the field to kill and loot over there. And you went there to kill and loot. But you didn't kill and loot. Is that what you're claiming?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What are you claiming?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I think we've been over this. We've been over this many times. Let's go on to something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Redacted. Yes. Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I hope we are not in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, this was in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You did speak about Hrtkovci then; right? And that a man was found killed in the field there; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, do you know that an investigation was conducted into that affair?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that. I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you know that that was the only incident that took place throughout that region, and do you know that after that the police was sent into Hrtkovci - Hrtkovci is a very small place with no police force - but the police were sent there to protect the place from people that could inflict this kind of harm against somebody there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the only killing, but it wasn't the only incident that took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. The only incident. Now, do you know that an investigation was conducted and that immediately afterwards the police were sent there to stay permanently and prevent any future incidents from taking place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that some policemen were sent there from Sremska Mitrovica, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. To protect and safeguard those people there. And were there any incidents after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The young man who led the unit from Sremska Mitrovica, he himself beat those people and mistreated them. I'm sure you know that too.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What did you say? Mistreated and beat the inhabitants?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What was his name? What was the name of this person who was sent there to protect and safeguard the population and then proceeded to beat and mistreat them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember his name, but I will do so. And the young man was sent back and he's still working in the police force today, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So are you really claiming that a policeman sent with a group of other policemen following an incident that took place to protect and safeguard that locality, to prevent any further violence, then engaged in the beating of the inhabitants? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. I won't belabour that point and comment further. I don't want to comment on things like that. It would be quite tasteless, out of place. Tell me this now, please: You said that you saw Seselj before a very difficult operation in the area of the Perucac lake near the electric powerplant. What kind of operation was there on the territory of Serbia? Tell me that. What was this operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We've already discussed that point. It was the hydroelectric powerplant, Peruca, where I was with my unit. We were stationed in Skelani, and then we went to Serbia. From Serbia, we crossed the dam. And from the Serb side, there were tanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. C-047, is it true that you went there of your own free will and that the police disarmed you and threw you out of the area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is absolutely not true. Absolutely incorrect. If you have information of that kind, then you must have information from the lake, and you know what went on there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Your answer suffices, as far as that matter is concerned. Now, you also say that in 1995 you escaped to Arkan in Erdut from Subotica, that you fled from Subotica to Erdut. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't flee. I went.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm just recapitulating what you said. You said that you had a conflict with the police in Subotica, a clash. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Because of that clash with the police force, you fled across the border into Eastern Slavonia; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I went to Belgrade first.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then to Erdut.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To Belgrade, to Ljutice Bogdana 1 Street and then we went on in a car.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And you then went to Erdut.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And what about Arkan's Volunteer Guards? Were they a component part of the Serbian Army of Krajina at that time? That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I assume it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you joined up. You joined the unit, which was under the composition of the Serbian Army of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did go there. That's quite true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And you yourself decided to leave Subotica because you clashed with the police there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, why should I ask anybody whether I should leave town or not? It's up to me. It depends on what I decide.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, that's what I say. It's up to you, your right to move around, and I assume that refers to any other citizen and inhabitant that decides to leave and become a volunteer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is every citizen's right to leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know how many thousands of Muslims left Sandzak like you did, yourself, to fight on the side of Alija Izetbegovic, for example?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know. Quite a lot of people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Were they perhaps sent by our police or government or something like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't say. I don't want to delve into those matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Tell me this, please: You say that it was quite by chance, so not in any combat operation, that you were wounded in November 1995.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a small injury.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right, a small injury. But you went to hospital.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, if you're talking about 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you were wounded in November 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This was just an injury. I twisted my foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But you were in hospital in November 1995, were you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in Vukovar to begin with and then in Subotica after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: How long did you stay in hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't. They just put a plaster cast on my leg.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. I see. And then they went to visit you, did they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then they told you that they were to go to Bosnia, to Sanski Most; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, right. Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That's what they told you in November 1995.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The officer whose nickname was Niski, he told me that. He was an officer of the Serbian Volunteer Guard, and his nickname was Niski. He was the one who told me that. He said that they were to go to Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I see, to Bosnia. And then he mentioned Sanski Most, did he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he did, yes. I think he mentioned Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that in November 1995 the Dayton Agreement was signed, that the war ceased on the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that it was signed. Now, whether war operations ceased, I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know of any war operations after November 1995, then? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right, fine.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: But later on I heard that a unit of the Serbian Guards were in fact in Sanski Most in 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, to be specific, you said you were there in November 1995 and that they told you that they were to go to Sanski Most and Bosnia in the coming period and it was at that time that the peace agreements were signed and that all operations ceased in the area. So that was your fabrication, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The unit withdrew in 1996, the Army of Yugoslavia, back to the barracks as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, linked to that, and immediately following that, you said that in Vukovar you saw one particular JNA unit. When did you see a JNA unit in Vukovar at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A JNA unit?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I saw the military police of the Kragujevac Corps in Leva Supoderica in 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right, in 1991. So what you want to say is when the JNA was throughout the territory of Yugoslavia, stationed, there, and you saw one particular unit in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just named one place, one location, and said there were there. Whereas, in Partizanska Street, I think it was the command and headquarters of the Novi Sad Corps that was stationed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Let's clear this point up. You saw the JNA in 1991; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, as this was immediate -- came immediately after your story about 1995, I linked this up to the year 1995 when it was impossible for you to see the JNA. Now, we've clarified this. You saw the JNA, in fact, in 1991; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That's a very useful explanation you've just given us. And what you indicated to us on the videotape, which does not refer actually to what you yourself saw but is an illustration of where Arkan, Hadic are in Vukovar in November 1991; that's it, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's the liberation of Vukovar -- or rather, after the fall of Vukovar. That's when that was taken, that footage.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It wasn't footage of an event you witnessed. All you did was to identify the two men; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in Vukovar after that, afterwards.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I just take a moment to consult my notes?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, you mention Ovcara, on page 11, paragraph 6 of your statement. Is it true that you do not have any knowledge about the events that took place in Vukovar at the -- after the factory farm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stated whom I heard this from, who told me about what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you spoke about what was rumoured; is that it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I give the name of the man who was very close to Milan Lancuzanin, Kameni, the Chetnik commander. And he told me. But I wasn't there, so I can't say myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you have no personal knowledge.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All you know is what you heard about.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, let me ask you this: Did you ever hear that the JNA had anything to do with Ovcara and the events at Ovcara?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What did you say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Which JNA unit had anything to do with the events in Ovcara?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Belgrade Guards unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And you claim that they were present in Ovcara when the crime took place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my information, both of them were there, the army and paramilitary, if you like to put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did that same man tell you that, the man that told you about who the perpetrators were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean? What are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The man who rallied these people up in Ovcara?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know from the media that it was the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Oh, I see. You've heard this from the media. That's how you come to know it. That's sufficient. Fine. That's enough for me. The fact that you know this from the media is not the subject of testimony here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You have five minutes left, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, Mr. May. Fine. I'm just trying to use my time as best as possible and to sort out the questions and select the ones I wish to ask, because I have a lot of material here. All sorts of untruths have been uttered here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You say that in Hrtkovci there was a unit from the composition of these special police units.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said that yourself a moment ago as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Was the police there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right, then. Of course it was there. Now, on page 12, paragraph 6, you state that it was under the command of Pera Skokandic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that the unit was from Sremska Mitrovica and that it was withdrawn. I think that this was replaced by the Novi Sad unit with this man at its head.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, the microphone was off.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think he was the commander of the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. And were they there to protect and safeguard the people from anything happening to them, to prevent an incident breaking out? Because you just mention this one man.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know what the police ought to have been doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But their assignment, did they carry it out or not? That's what I'm asking you now.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think they did it to the best of their ability, as it should have been carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, is this the same man, Skokandic, who was the deputy of the president of the reformist party in Vojvodina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So he mistreated the citizens of Hrtkovci; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not him. I mentioned the Sremska Mitrovica unit that was replaced.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What I'm asking you now, you say that there were some people there from Novi Sad. Were they safeguarding and protecting the people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the Novi Sad unit was protecting these locals of Hrtkovci. The few men that stayed on, I assume that they protected the people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. The few of them who remained, as you put it. Now, you say that in Subotica you saw Serb -- houses of non-Serbs marked with a cross of some kind, and you say this on page 13, paragraph 3. You mention that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It says in Hrtkovci, not Subotica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Hrtkovci.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I refer to Hrtkovci in this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, is the population mostly non-Serb?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, in Hrtkovci, were the houses marked in this way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They weren't marked like that, but there were other incidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What incidents? You say that the cathedral in Subotica was blown up.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The doors to the cathedral.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In your statement, you say that the cathedral was bombed and blown up.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the doors are a part of the cathedral.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, some person motivated by political motives placed an explosive device at the door. Is there a difference between that and blowing up the cathedral?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's all the same thing, because the doors are part of the building. They were enormous, large wooden heavy doors.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, do you know that an investigation was conducted with respect to this offence and that criminal proceedings were launched against the perpetrators of that crime and that they were condemned for this act and that they weren't members of the Serbian Radical Party at all, by the way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So actually, you don't know anything about the whole thing.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. But I think I know who the perpetrators were. And when the bomb was planted on -- at the school in Velegija Street. I know about that, and who planted the bomb there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: My question to you was: Do you know that an investigation was conducted and that the perpetrators were brought to justice, that they were found guilty of the offence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And you don't know that they weren't even members of the Serbian Radical Party?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: This must be your last question now.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I do have a few other matters to ask with respect to these alleged explosions in Subotica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: If a bomb wasn't thrown at any Hungarian school but the Svetozar Markovic school, which was a general school regardless of ethnic affiliation.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The school was in Velegija Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you know that a group of young people, young men, among whom was this Bojanic whom you accuse, was hit by a shrapnel in the school -- on the school premises when somebody threw a bomb?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wasn't somebody. It was him. He threw the bomb.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you know that the plaque bearing the name of the poet Geza Kostolany [phoen], a Hungarian poet, in fact, a local of those regions, which was placed on the wall of the school building, was not damaged at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't, because the bomb wasn't placed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But you said that they planted a bomb to blow up the plaque with this poet's name on it, and it wasn't damaged at all.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. The time is now up. Mr. Tapuskovic, have you questions for this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do have questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. After the adjournment. We'll adjourn now, 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask you to pay attention to tab 21, 458.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I would kindly like to ask for private session. Briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So, Witness, if you did the work you did, like many other types of work that I know - and this pertained to them too - were you able to be in this particular line of work without being a member of the Communist Party at the same time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had to be a member of the Communist Party.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So you were a member of the Communist Party?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And you joined the Radical Party, as you put it, precisely because you wanted to do away with the members of the Communist Party that were supposed to be overthrown.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I lived from this work, and I was a member of the Communist Party for five years only.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And after that you decided to do what you decided to do, to struggle against this same Communist Party that practically supported you and on whose income you lived.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Any political orientation was different, but this was a job I did and that I lived on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: At any rate, in respect to the war, when war was mentioned in 1991, it was said that the monarchists had to do away with the communists.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please explain to the Trial Chamber a few things that have to do with Kosovo. I'm now going to mention the work that you did. In your statement, in the statement you gave here, and in the statement that you gave to the investigators, I see that due to your work, you were in Kosovo for a rather long period of time, between 1985 and 1989, and then in 1988 too, and after 1990; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You said here: "I remember that in 1988 there was a big clash in Priluzje where several Kosovo Albanian demonstrators and two to three Serbian policemen got killed." So is it correct that in these clashes in 1988 three Serb policemen were killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so. I don't know whether it was two or three, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Is it also correct that in this period of time, before 1989, there were quite a few other such incidents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you give us at least an approximation of the number of policemen who were victims in the clashes between the police and the demonstrators between 1985 and 1989? Can you give us an approximation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there were quite a few, but I don't actually know the number of policemen killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: At any rate, these were actions aimed against the -- terrorist attacks launched against the police and the citizenry, in that period of time, between 1985 and 1990?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did this happen after 1990 as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Precisely due to these terrorist actions, were Serbs migrating from these areas? Were they leaving Kosovo under pressure between 1985 and 1990 and after 1990?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And do you know that in these periods of time, between 1985 and 1990 and after 1990, there was a considerable number of emigres from Albania who came from Albania to Serbia and settled there, although they were not citizens of that country?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Was that a considerable number?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In the documents of your party, the number mentioned is 300.000 persons.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number, but I know that such persons were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now I would like us to have a look at something together, these documents, that is. And could you please explain to the Trial Chamber some things in relation to this document. This document was shown to you by the Prosecutor. This is Exhibit 458, tab 2. And it has to do with the programme declaration of the Serb Radical Party for 1991. Would you please have a look at this. The Prosecutor showed you paragraph 2, paragraph 3, I think paragraph 1 too. But please look at this first sentence. It is an introduction to the entire document. It says: "On the basis of the programme and the statute adopted at the founding assembly in Kragujevac on the 23rd of February, 1991"; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And then further on towards the end: "The Serb Radical Party" - this is what it says here - "as it acts as an eminently democratic organisation under the conditions of a multi-party system and having opted for peaceful methods only, as regards political struggle, proclaims its political objectives." This was in February 1991. So at that moment was any reference made to the following, that these objectives should be attained by peaceful means; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so. This is just on paper. But it was quite different.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So what, communists and monarchists were supposed to have a showdown already then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Chetnik units were being established throughout Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: For the monarchists to settle accounts with the communists?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In all of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Serbia and Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I would be interested in the following, Article 25. The Prosecutor showed you this in the programme of the Serb Radical Party, that expulsions should take place straight away, that is, the beginning of 1991. All 360.000 Albanian emigres. So these were only people who were staying in Serbia. That is what was done by all civilised countries in the world when there are no proper conditions for this, that emigres who do not have the citizenship of the country concerned should be expelled from the country where they live.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not a politician, but I think Vojislav Seselj wrote this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: But these are the people who emigrated from Albania, came to Yugoslavia, stayed there for decades, for years, without having citizenship.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a considerable number of them. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to draw the attention of the Trial Chamber to tab 3. And that is the statute of the Serb Radical Party. You know that the first statute was adopted in March 1991; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.
