utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And this is an amendment that was adopted on the 30th of January, 1994; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Now, please look at Article 87. That's the last article. There's a translation of this too. This was adopted by the Third Congress of the Serb Radical Party which was held in Belgrade on the 30th of January, 1994; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's when the Serb Radical Party was registered.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the Honourable Judges please focus on this, on page -- on the last page of the Serb version of this statute, because it says "Agreement on cooperation," and that part had not been translated. But it is written in a language that the witness knows very well. I have a photocopy of this. Could the witness please look at this document. It is in tab 3. And I would like to ask the witness something in this connection.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you can see here -- you can see here that the photograph is missing. You can't see it. But it says "Doctors on the move. Dr. Vojislav Seselj and Dr. Milan Babic." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And then underneath that -- well, the statute was changed on the 30th of January, 1994. And then it says here, "In Belgrade, on the 2nd of February, a joint press conference was held of Dr. Milan Babic and Dr. Vojislav Seselj. It was publicly stated that the two most significant parties in the territory of Srpska Krajina made an agreement in order to promote their joint political objectives that promote the priority state interests of the Serb people in the Republika Srpska, the Republika Srpska Krajina, in order to have stable conditions for the operation of its government authorities." That is what Babic stated after the agreement was signed. Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about that. Although, I was not doing this in 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And do you know that after they signed this agreement in 1994, Seselj said - and I read - "Dr. Seselj said that for the continuation of the coalition was of decisive importance was that the interests of the SRS and the SDS of Republika Srpska and Republika Srpska Krajina coincided, that is to say, that all the Serb territories should become part of one state." Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Was this an agreement between Babic and Seselj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So you know about that. And after that, what happened was that the Serb Radical Party joined the government in the territory of the Republika Srpska Krajina.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I'll put three tabs together. I would just like to read part of tab 11. And this same question pertains to what it says in tab 16 and in tab 18. However, I would kindly like to ask the Trial Chamber to look at tab 11, the last sentence. You have stated your views with regard to this document, but this is what the last sentence says. It was signed by Vojvoda Mirko Blagojevic. It says: "The Serb Chetniks will truly and honourably fight for the freedom of Republika Srpska and its international affirmation within the Army of Republika Srpska." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So it is said within the Army of Republika Srpska. And these other two documents do not make any reference to the Yugoslav People's Army. Quite explicitly, in none of these documents is there any mention of the Yugoslav People's Army or of the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there is no mention sir, but they were present at the frontline.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will finish very fast. I have nothing else in this connection. Now I need tab 15. In tab 15 - and the Prosecution did not show the witness tab 15 - but this is the third document in this tab. I would just like to show the witness what it says here. You said, Witness, what happened in Hrtkovci in 1992; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't want to take you back to that, but tell me first: How many refugees during 1991 came from areas outside Serbia, from Bosnia, Slavonia, to Serbia, during 1991, primarily in Vojvodina where you live. Was it a considerable number?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a considerable number.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you give us an approximate figure?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot give you a figure.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: This is what it says on the document: "On the 11th of and 12th -- on the 11th of December, 1991, a column of refugees on tractors moved through Western Slavonia from Okucani towards Banja Luka. The refugees are on the tractors. Down the entire frontline which was held by the Banja Luka Corps the situation was very difficult." Are you aware of such information about refugees moving in this way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I am aware of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Oh, you are aware of this document too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you just one more thing: In answer to a question from the Prosecutor, you spoke about mosques destroyed. I am familiar with that, and I'm sure there is data about this. But could you tell me: In addition to Catholic churches, Roman Catholic churches and mosques, do you know at all how many churches were destroyed in the areas of Croatia, Krajina, Slavonia, Bosnia? Do you know whether any churches were destroyed and how many?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I didn't mention mosques, but I do know that many churches were destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: How many were destroyed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very few remained standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, if you could help me with this. It's about the agreement on cooperation between Mr. Seselj and Milan Babic. Does it appear at the last page of the statute on the Serbian Radical Party? Because I didn't bring my B/C/S version of that. Is it a kind of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Official Gazette?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour Kwon, the statute was published in the only journal that existed over there, and that was called Greater Serbia, Velika Serbia. And it was published by editors who represented the Radical Party. And in that journal, Velika Serbia, this statute was published. It may have been published somewhere else. And you have the translation of that statute up to Article 87. And in that article, it says that "The statute was adopted on the 30th of January, 1994," and already on the 2nd of February this agreement was reached between Babic and Seselj. After the peace negotiations, after the Vance-Owen Plan, that is, three years after the peace talks had ended.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. I got it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. You did in fact refer to tab 15 I see from my notes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I did, Your Honour. And I have a few questions that -- a few clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And the first one is actually in -- I would like to have closed session. The rest one in -- private session right now.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have actually discussed here during the cross-examination of both Mr. Milosevic and Mr. Tapuskovic, we had discussed the statement that the witness did. I suggest that we exhibit it or at least mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. We have a vast amount of paper, and the fewer statements we can have exhibited the better. Is there any particular reason why we need this one?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, I only thought because we referred so often and you may want to check. No, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, Mr. Milosevic put to you that Seselj was imprisoned in autumn 1990 and therefore you could not have met him, as you have explained. And you would like to put to you, therefore, an article. And we have prepared the article. It's an article called "Duke Seselj free again." Could that be provided.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, in the English translation, there is no date.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: But, witness, if you look at the Serbian version, is that an article of the 16th of November, 1990? And can you tell us which newspaper it is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I see that it is the Borba newspaper, a newspaper published in Belgrade. And the date is the 16th of November, 1990.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And in this first paragraph, I quote now, it says: "After 26 days spent in prison, Duke Dr. Vojislav Seselj, independent presidential candidate, is free again on probation." And my question to you is: Did you meet him after the 16th of November or was it rather in September or October? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was before he went to prison.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to have this exhibited.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Prosecution Exhibit 458, tab 26.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In relation to the SRS party, Mr. Milosevic put to you that it did not exist in 1990 and also not in the beginning of 1991. And you said as an answer to this, "It existed, but under a different name." And I would like now to put again to you the statute of the Serbian Radical Party of 1994 that we had just discussed -- that you had just discussed with Mr. Tapuskovic. And I would like you to look at Article 5, the first two paragraphs. It says here: "The party is the legal successor of the Serbian Freedom Movement and the Serbian Chetnik Movement. The initiative to form the Serbian Freedom Movement came on 6th of January, 1990 in Belgrade from a group of citizens who signed the founding manifesto." Hearing this name, Serbian Freedom Movement, is that a name you are familiar with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is what I had in mind when I was referring to this other name -- or rather, the first name of the Serbian Radical Party. From this Serbian Freedom Movement, the Serbian Radical Party developed. And the Serbian Chetnik Movement existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In relation to the statute of the SRS party, Mr. Milosevic also put to you that it didn't have a structure with provinces. And I would like you -- to refer you now to paragraph -- to Article 58 of that same statute. And it says here: "The parties organised in all Serbian lands, regions, municipalities, and populated areas as well as abroad." And in Article 62, it also speaks about "regional boards are formed by special decisions of the administration." Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of that. That is how we formed it in Subotica.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And Your Honour, I would like to put to you --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What is it, Mr. Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that the question is inappropriate because I didn't claim that they didn't have their branches in various areas. But what I claimed was that no presidency of the Serbian Radical Party or Vojvodina existed. As the witness indicated in the diagram in tab 4, where it says "The presidency of the Serbian Radical Party of Vojvodina, Maja Gojkovic, president of the presidency."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So that is what I was claiming.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. You can't make another speech now. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In this same context, I would like to have displayed to the witness an article related to the person Mirko Blagojevic, the Vojvoda that you have mentioned and that Mr. Milosevic also had mentioned. And it is an article in Oslobodjenje, 5th of March, 1991, referring to Mirko Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And you see, actually, in the first paragraph how he said, "Aside from Dr. Vojislav Seselj, president of the Serbian Radical Party, and Mirko Blagojevic, president of the regional board of this party for north-eastern Bosnia. Do you recall that you had these structures and presidents of these regional structures?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were, quite certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In the examination-in-chief, you had mentioned that there was a VJ unit with the name Kobras in Vukovar which you saw when you were in the hospital there. With Mr. Milosevic, you discussed the JNA units present in Vukovar, but you spoke only about the year 1991. And my question to you is: When did you see the members of the Kobra unit? Which year?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was hurt in the Guards. That would be 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic put to you the point that you left Zvornik. And I was a little bit puzzled about this. Did you ever fight in Zvornik, or is that just a misunderstanding?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a misunderstanding. I was at the Bajina Basta Perucac hydro powerplant. And I didn't go to Zvornik. Units of the Army of Yugoslavia were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And my last question relates to the situation in Kosovo in the year 1988. And Mr. Tapuskovic put to you that the police was engaged there in relation to terrorist activities. And my question to you is: What exactly did you do? What did you -- what were you against? What were you doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a member of the police force, I had to go there. I spent there a month and a half. There were demonstrations by the Albanians, the Siptars, at the crossroads between Titova Mitrovica and Pristina Roads. The police arrived with TABs, armoured vehicles, helicopters. There were heavy machine-guns on these TABs. And this was in Priluzje. So I had to go there on assignment. I received such orders.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, this concludes my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Witness C-047, that concludes your evidence. You are now free to go. Thank you for coming to the International Tribunal to give your evidence. I'm sorry that you've been detained here so long to give it and had to come back. Thank you. If you'd just wait while the blinds are put down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: While we are waiting for the next witness, may I raise an administrative matter with the Prosecution. My question is whether the Prosecution would be able to produce a detailed index of the Prosecution's exhibit produced to the Court so far, including the -- all the tabs of each binder so that we can make an electronic search. So if you could pass on my words to Mr. Nice and --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That shouldn't be a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And update them from time to time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And may I now also mention that we have as the next witness the Witness C-017. He had been granted protective measures of pseudonym and image distortion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If I can just raise a matter, Your Honours? I've just been looking at the exhibits for C-017. I notice at tab 9 that there's an entire statement from this witness included within the exhibit bundle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, we'll have to -- we'll have to see about the admissibility of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: As to why it should be. It's not normally the practise, of course, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, to exhibit the witness's statement unless there's some particular reason for it.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And it's only a proposal. The -- the problem that arose was during the preparation of the testimony, the witness read his past statement and found a lot of inaccuracies. And he mentioned which it was and what should be the right wording. And that's actually the -- this declaration that he made with our help, of course; we typed it up. And we can see whether it's necessary to exhibit it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, we'll see whether that's necessary or not. We've got it at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Let the witness take the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you'd like to take a seat now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, could we have the first about 10 to 15 minutes in private session. And as soon as we are in private session, I would explain why.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It's actually from the atlas, but we have highlighted together with the help of the witness certain areas that the witness will refer to during his testimony. And we do not need to explain any details right now. It's just that the witness should have it in front of him if he wants to show something.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: The only thing you should tell us: Buna, what was it and where was it situated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: It's 12 kilometres from Mostar, and it's marked here with a "D."

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Before the war, what kind of a place was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Buna is a tourist place, generally speaking. And the camp was a tourist camp, in fact, or a camp for foreign citizens, foreigners.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And during the war, what was it, during the time you were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: My first encounter with the camp during the war was when it was a base for those people who came in.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Which -- a base for which troops? Who was there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: What I saw when I arrived was a group of criminals wearing uniforms. And there were all kinds, in fact. There were Seselj's men, Seselj Chetniks, the White Eagles, the Red Berets, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you, with some technical help from the Prosecutor's Office, prepare a sketch of the layout of the camp Buna?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And can we now have tab 1 on Sanction. Your Honours, we'll --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honours, we'll go now through the tabs and would need a -- an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: An exhibit number, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 460.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Tab 1, is that the layout of the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Where would the -- these uniformed people that you mentioned, where would they sleep? Where would they be housed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: They slept in the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: But where there? I mean, you have indicated buildings. Would they sleep in the bungalows?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes, because the camp consisted of bungalows and an area for tents. And when I arrived, they were actually in the bungalows, but some of them were also in the hotel at the Buna.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And was there a kind of an administration in the camp, where the commanders would sit? Where would they be?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes, there was. Mirko Simic was also in the camp, and at that time he was one of the main people or number-one man for Herzegovina for the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Where would Mr. Simic be in the camp? Did he have an office there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes, he did. He occupied one of the bungalows, but I really can't remember which.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And Mr. Simic, how did you get to know him? Did you have dealings with him when you were in the camp? Did you see him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: I did see him around, but I had absolutely no idea who he was until I was told.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And you said that he was -- he was a leading -- a leading figure in the SDS. How would you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Well, when I arrived - I have to say this again - I didn't know who he was at all. But during one of the operations after Mostar, which they referred to as cleansing, I learnt that as that man had issued orders for -- to the local chief of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, we need to go briefly into private session to discuss a point.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: While you were in this position, did you observe the killing of the Croat, Pavo Gagro?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you explain to us what you saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And when you say three or four of them, whom do you mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: I mean the men wearing those uniforms; that is to say, Seselj's Chetniks.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And what else happened to Gagro? You say they were kicking him.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: They kept kicking Gagro from his house to the hotel, which is a little less than 1 kilometre away, and he died as a result. He died during the kicking.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned the Seselj Chetniks. Was there any sort of a commander among them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes, there was. However, at that point in time, I had no idea who they were or who their commander was. I learnt all that later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And who was their commander? What did you learn later on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: When this was happening, I saw a man leave Pavo Gagro's house with a bag, and later on I learnt that his name was Svabo. I saw him then and never again. And later on I learnt that he was the man who was in command there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You said they were Seselj's Chetniks. How did you know that? What did they look like and how could you identify them later on, later on as Seselj's Chetniks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Well, as I said, when I arrived I had no idea who they were. However, later on during the time I spent in the camp, I saw their IDs and I learnt from the stories they told that they were in fact Seselj's volunteers or Chetniks, whatever you like to call them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to show now on the -- on the screen a few patches. And they're actually from Exhibit 349, the binder with all the patches. And I have here the first patch that I would like to show you. It's tab 12. You see here a patch with a wolf. What -- what kind of a patch -- is that patch familiar to you, and who was having such a patch?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: I saw this patch for the first time when I arrived at the camp at Buna. And this is the insignia worn by the members of the Red Berets, with a brown wolf on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And now tab 11. Did you see people with such a patch?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Once again, I first saw it at the Buna camp. And once again, this was worn by members of the Red Berets.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And as some of us here in the courtroom cannot read Cyrillic, can you say what it mean, these words?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: It says here "Milicija Krajina."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Or "police Krajina.". Interpreter's note.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And then the next patch. It's tab 13. Is that familiar with you, and what does it say on the patch and who wore it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: This is another patch that I saw at the camp. It was worn by the Chetniks, Seselj's Chetniks, and the White Eagles. And I'd see this patch many times subsequently. You could quite simply buy it in the streets. And it says "Headquarters or main staff Serb Chetnik Movement."

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And just you mention it was worn by Seselj's Chetniks and the White Eagles. What is the difference between the two? Could you distinguish them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: I wasn't able to distinguish between them when I arrived. The only thing I could see was the difference between them and the Red Berets. It was only later on that I learnt and became aware of the fact that they were in fact two groups, that one of them were Seselj's Chetniks and the others were the White Eagles.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: The White Eagles belonged to which organisation, which party or founder?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: All I can say on that score is that I heard they belonged to Jovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: While you were still in that same position, having observed the killing of Gagro, did you see a military officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Could you repeat that question, be more specific? An officer of what?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Oh, that. Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. What did you see? What happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: What I myself saw -- I didn't know who he was, actually, or what he was -- but a man turned up wearing a camouflage uniform of the Yugoslav People's Army, and he automatically began screaming right at the entrance to the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What was he screaming?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: He screamed out, "Who sent you here?"

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What was -- what answer did he get?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: The first answer he received - and I could hear that because Kusic was right close by - Kusic said, "You know very well who sent us."

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And did any other Red Berets join those two at some point in time?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "Who sent them?" Interpreter's note.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Across the road from the camp, in front of the school building, a man stood there whose name I learnt -- later learnt was Boro Todorovic. Now, whether from the front side or the back side, another man turned up, whom I didn't know International Committee of the Red Cross but his name was Aco Legija, and he began talking to Perisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Those two that you just mentioned, were they Red Berets or were they JNA? Who were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: They were members of the Red Berets.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What did they speak about with the officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Well, first of all, Aco Legija swore at him and then said that he knew who sent them there very well. And as there were three men standing there with him, Njegos Kusic started having an argument with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What kind of an argument?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Well, as to who had sent them. Njegos Kusic for the first time said he would call Frenki up and then he would see who had sent them there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: This reference to Frenki, did it mean anything to you? Did you know what he was -- to whom he was referring?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: No, never heard of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And this person, this JNA officer, did he have a high rank? Could you see it? And did you later on learn who he was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes. Later on I learnt who that was. But I saw him for the first time on that occasion. He did have a rank of some kind, but I don't remember what exactly at the time. But he was Momcilo Perisic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we just briefly display the photo, tab 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And is that the person you mentioned and you later met?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's a photo of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: This is a convenient time. We'll adjourn now. Witness C-017, in this break and any other breaks there may be in your evidence, could you remember not to speak to anybody about it until it's over and not to let anybody speak to you about it, and that does include the Prosecution too. Very well. It's something for the senior legal officer, please. Twenty minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, if this court isn't required this afternoon, we'll sit until 2.00 in order to make up some time.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you have described this dispute between Momcilo Perisic and the three Red Berets. How did the dispute end?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: What I described is what happened right before me. After that, they left either to one of the bungalows or wherever. But at any rate, I couldn't see them any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You have mentioned the -- the Chetniks, their patches. What kind of uniforms did they have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: As I've already pointed out, this was a group of criminals that were gathered from here and there and everywhere. They did not have any kind of uniforms that would show that they belonged to a particular unit or formation. There were JNA uniforms there. There were NATO-made uniforms or whatever you wish to call them. There were even some people who wore civilian jackets or civilian trousers. At any rate, it was a mix of all sorts of things.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: The days that followed your arrival, what did you see them do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: All the entire settlement had been looted, the entire settlement at the Buna. As far as I managed to see from this camp - and I did see the houses later - the houses that had been looted. Also there were stolen cars there. I mean, quite simply they stopped people in the road and took their cars.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And you have described the -- the patches that you saw on the Red Berets. What kind of uniforms did they wear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: The Red Berets had American-made uniforms, all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What was the relation between the Red Berets and the Chetniks? Was there anyone in superior -- was any group superior to the other?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Well, in this entire mess - and I already explained that when I arrived there, I realised it was an unorganised group - but after a while, one could see that the Red Berets dominated over the Chetniks and that the man who was truly in charge was Aco Legija.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Aco Legija is -- has he anything to do with the deputy commander of the Arkan's with that same name, or is it a different Aco Legija?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: No. It's a completely different person.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you prepare a chart, a chart -- a name chart with the people that you met in the course of two Red Beret camps? Did you prepare a chart with the help of the Prosecutor indicating the name and the description of the person and what you learnt about this person?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And Your Honours, it's tab 2 of the Exhibit 460.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you -- did you give all these names of the people that you met and their details?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, I do not intend to go through each and every person on this list, but those who really are important we will address specifically.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Those -- I forgot to ask you: How many of these Chetniks were in the Buna camp and how many of the Red Berets, to your recollection?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: I really cannot say how many there were exactly, because there was major disarray there. However, at any rate, there were more Chetniks than Red Berets.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Those Red Berets that you saw, were they all from this original Red Berets, as you mentioned, that were trained in Knin, or were they also from different regions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: No. Absolutely all of those who were there and who I saw were members of the first 57, according to what they said themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did they tell -- did they speak about where they had been before, in which regions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes, they did. They did so often.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What did they say? Where had they been before coming to Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: I cannot remember everything, but most of the stories I heard were from Pero Divljak, like I mentioned in my statement. They told me that they had been in Borovo Selo, I can remember that, for instance. Then Knin, then Baranja, then Okucani, and also Plitvice. Those are some of the places I can remember from what they told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And those Seselj's Chetniks, where -- what did they say they had been?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: I did not have many contacts with Seselj Chetniks. This is a group that was unavoidable, because they were all over the place, but it was not a good thing to be near them. However, I managed to find out later on, primarily from the Red Berets, that all of them, all of Seselj's Chetniks, had 27 days of training under the Red Berets at the camp in Golubic and that they had also been in Borovo Selo.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to go into private session just for a very brief question.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You said -- you mentioned already the attack on Mostar. When did it take place? Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. When?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall the attack on Mostar. It was on the 6th of May. And the 6th of May is Djurdjevdan, a holiday, St. George's Day.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And we are talking about 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Those that were in the Buna camp, the Chetniks and the Red Berets, did they take part in this attack on Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Where were you taken from Buna, to where in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: From Buna, we went to the barracks called Juzni Logor, southern camp. From where the attack was launched.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Are these JNA barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes. As I already said, at that time the JNA was still in existence, and this is JNA barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Were JNA troops involved in the attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Which units, to your knowledge? Which units were involved?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: What I can say with certainty, as far as the JNA units are concerned, was that the right flank was held by the members of the 63rd Airborne Brigade, and on the side where I was there were all sorts of things, because there were quite a few JNA reservists there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And looking at the map that we had in the beginning, when you say "right flank," what -- what river bank do you mean? "Right flank," what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: I'm referring to the river.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. So the right bank in the direction -- from the direction of Sarajevo or in the direction of Sarajevo? Which is the right bank?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: For me, there are no banks. But this is the way Karadzic viewed things from Sarajevo, so from his vantage point it was the left bank, looking from Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Just put it on the ELMO briefly and show it to us, yes, so that we are not confused about where the -- where the 63rd Airborne Brigade was and where you and the people from Buna were. You have to show it on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please -- could you please show it again.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: The side where I was, this is the side where I was. Viewed from Sarajevo, it's the left bank. And viewed from here, it's the right bank. Members of the 63rd Airborne Brigade were on this side. And I, together with the others, was on this other side here.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The witness was pointing on the right side -- where the "D" is actually. It's easiest to see. He was on the side where Buna is and the Red Berets on the other side. Yes. Thank you. That's -- Airborne, yes, the 63rd Airborne Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Were any local TO forces involved in this military activity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And any police units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: With whom did the local TO and the police cooperate? On which side were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: The local police and Territorial Defence were on the side where I was, so that is to say the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Who was in charge -- in overall charge of the attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: As far as I know, the operations in the area, in the field actually, were led by Rade Mihajlovic. Above him were Cvetkovic and Malijevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And who was in overall command of all troops? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Momcilo Perisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Who gave assignments to your unit? Your direct superior was who?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Aco Legija.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: While the attack was ongoing - and I do not want to go in any details of the attack as such - did you observe what was done with civilians the troops came across?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What did you see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Well, I saw when they were taking them out of the basements. I saw them kill a man who was almost 80 years old. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see any -- any looting or burning of properties?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes, I did. Everything was looted and torched, everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see anything involving a doctor and his family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What happened to the doctor and his family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: I don't know what happened later, but what I saw was the doctor was shot in the leg.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Who did that and why?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Kizo did the shooting. He was allegedly looking for a sniper.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Kizo is who? To which group does he belong?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Kizo belonged to Seselj's Chetniks.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: The doctor, did he actually have a gun? And was he involved, to your knowledge, in any fighting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Where did that take place? Was it outside or was it in the home of the doctor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: It was in the doctor's home, his apartment, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you observe the killing of a Croatian citizen called Cvitanovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. What happened to this person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: This man was captured in civilian clothes. He was captured by the Serbian forces. First they beat him. Then they put him into a ditch and threw a hand grenade in.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did a TV crew come to this scene?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes, shortly after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Then the locals showed the TV crew the corpse, and they said that they wanted to show them what the Croat forces were doing to Serb civilians.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, we need to go into private session briefly for the next event.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: When you arrived in Rotimlja, did you see anything involving civilians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What did you see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Well, when we arrived up there, people in civilian clothing were lined up in two lines. They were apart from each other. In one line were Croats, and in the other line were Muslims. After that, Pejanovic, this captain, made a speech to them. He said that they were on Serb land and since Croats had been killing Serbs for years and for centuries, they had no business on Serb land, while the Muslims could remain if they were to be loyal to the Serb authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And did the Croats leave? Do you know? To your knowledge.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: As far as I know, the Croats were transferred to the prison in Bileca.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: The Muslims stayed behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did the -- the Chetniks and the Red Berets from the Buna camp also take part in an attack on the village Bijelo Polje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And were you joined -- while doing that, were you joined by other troops? If so, which?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes. On the road leading to Bijelo Polje -- rather, the road on which we were supposed to go, we met up with a unit called Vukovarci, the men from Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What kind of unit was that? A regular army unit or what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: No, this was not a regular army unit. These were men who had been at the frontline in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: If not a regular army unit, what -- what were they -- to which groups were they related to? Were they Chetniks, or were they police? Can -- if you don't know, that's fine. But maybe you know.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: What I can say with certainty is that this is a paramilitary formation. It was brought to Herzegovina by Novica Gusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Were any TO or JNA units involved in this attack on the village Bijelo Polje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes. Again, the same person, Rade Mihajlovic, and the same territorials too, or almost the same, from the surrounding Serb villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have air support during the attack, air support of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What happened to the village and the villagers during the attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: I don't know what happened to them, because when we entered the village, the village was totally empty.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And what about the -- did the looting take place and burning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes, it did. These are things that such people invariably do.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see the murder of an old man? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Who did it and how was he murdered?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Well, he was murdered by Pero Divljak. First he cut off his ears, then threw him into a pool, and then he threw bricks at him until he drowned.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did the JNA withdraw from Mostar in June 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did Momcilo Perisic give a speech in relation to this withdrawal? And if so, what did he say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes, he did. Momcilo Perisic made a speech at the airfield in front of everybody who happened to be there, in front of everybody who was there. He said that Mostar was sold for Doboj and Derventa, that his hands were tied, that this was a political game, that he couldn't do a thing, and that the only thing he could do was that he could leave weapons to those who would stay behind; whereas, those who would come along with him could become soldiers on a contractual basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And did you understand what that meant?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Not quite, but I gathered that what he said, that is, that he would make it possible for them to become professional soldiers, that this applied to people who were born in Bosnia. So either they could go with him or they could stay where they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did the Red Berets take weaponry and vehicles from the army, from the JNA, during this withdrawal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes, they did; the Red Berets and all the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: At the time of the withdrawal, did you see a massacre at the Neretva River?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, we will need to go into private session just for one question. And in this context, we also have to put tab 4 on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, this big facility that we see where we have that circle, is that the north camp, a JNA facility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: When the -- what was the JNA doing at that time? Where were the JNA units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: As I have already said, there was all-out panic because the JNA was withdrawing.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Where did the massacre occur?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: As far as I am able to say, it was on the Neretva River bank.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Is that where there is a circle indicated and underneath is "Bakijina Luka"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And there is -- what did you -- what did you see happen? When did you first notice it and what did you see?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, if you could turn off your microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: But there's no voice distortion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Oh, that was a mistake, I think.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From there, as I was told to go and see what was happening on the other side of the river. So right next to the river there were bunkers. And as I didn't want to be shot at from the other side, I climbed onto the building and from that building the first thing I saw was people in a column escorted by men in camouflage uniforms were crossing the road in the direction of the Neretva River.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And what did you see then happen?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [redacted] When I saw that they were in a column escorted by men in camouflage uniform, it bode nothing good. I followed them with my binoculars as far as the river bank, and as I looked at the bank there was another group of men there in camouflage uniforms who were already killing civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you recognise anyone doing this killing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I recognised Pero Divljak and somebody called Vranjanac.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Vranjanac, to which group did he belong?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Vranjanac belonged to Seselj's Chetniks.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: How could you recognise Divljak and him? Do they look particular?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: First because Pero Divljak was with me for no longer than 20 or 30 minutes before that. We were together. And he's the only one who is over 2 metres tall, and Vranjanac is also quite tall, but I recognised him by the way in which he held his rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And you mentioned that those -- those people that were killed came from a particular neighbourhood. Which neighbourhood is that and what kind of people from their ethnicity were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: The people were mostly Muslims, and they were from the neighbourhood of Zalik. I don't know where they rounded them up, whether it was from shelters or their apartments. I don't know that. But anyway, they were from the neighbourhood called Zalik.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see Divljak and Vranjanac later on? And if so, what did they look like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: I can't remember about Vranjanac. I do remember Pero Divljak. It is one of the images I'm trying to forget, because Pero Divljak wore a uniform that was totally soaked in blood.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I would now like to go into private session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: The Nevesinje Brigade, as you said, is that a -- a brigade of the JNA, or is it the VRS? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: At that point in time, when this was happening, I had no idea. However, that brigade later existed as the Herzegovina Brigade of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In Nevesinje, did you see again the Red Berets and the Chetniks from the Buna camp? And if so, where were they staying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes, I did meet them, at the hotel in Nevesinje.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see any JNA troops? And if so, where were they staying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes, there were some JNA troops, but they were in the process of withdrawing.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And which corps? Would you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, judging by what people said, it was the Uzice Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did the Red Berets and the Chetniks, did they cooperate with the police or the TO in the -- in Nevesinje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In which way did they cooperate? Where were they? Were they ...?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: They did cooperate. As far as I can remember, there were several meetings that I saw headed by Novica Gusic, Aco Legija, Vranjanac, Miroslav Duka, Krsto Savic, all of them were there. I saw meetings, what they spoke about, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And did you see this person Duka whom you mentioned was the commander of the Herzegovina police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And you mentioned a Krsto Savic. Who was he? What was his position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes, I mentioned Krsto Savic. He was commander of the police station in Nevesinje.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned before in your testimony the group Vukovarci. Were they also in Nevesinje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did these -- did all these troops, did they conduct any operations in Nevesinje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: I spent a very short time in Nevesinje, but while I was there Nevesinje was totally cleansed of Muslims. The group that did this and boasted of this was a group of Vukovarci, commanded by Crni.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see any -- any signs of this cleansing of Muslims? What did they do? What did you see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: The only thing I saw were people in a bus, that is, women and children. And I learnt later from what others said that they were sent to Trebinje and then from there to Macedonia. But that is only what I heard from others. I just saw the busses, nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see any looting or burning of houses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: On one occasion, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What did you see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: I saw Krsto Savic and the others who were with him when they killed Redzo Trebovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Is that -- was that a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see how they killed him and what happened to his property?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: [redacted] [redacted], the house had already been set on fire, the house that he was in, as was the house across the road, a new house owned by Redzo Trebovic, which they had already started looting. All I know is that they said that Redzo was inside -- rather, Krsto bragged that Redzo was inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And Redzo, did he have a position? Who was he? You said he was a Muslim, but did he have a position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: What I learnt -- I had never been in Nevesinje before that in my life, but what I learnt from stories was that Redzo Trebevic was one of the wealthiest Muslims in Nevesinje and he held a position in the SDA, according to what they said.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did the Red Berets set up a training camp in the village Borci and start training there in July 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, on this map, there is a "C" indicated where Borci is located.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What was the name of this camp and what was it before and then during the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: What the name of the camp was, I really don't know. But it is on the Boracko Lake. It was a tourist facility which was mainly used for tourist purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And you have made a sketch with the help of technical staff of the Prosecutor's Office of this camp; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And it's tab 6, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Is that the sketch that you made?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And who used this camp? Who was -- who was housed there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: As I said, I spent a very short time in Nevesinje. And once we arrived at Borci, the camp had already been established and the Red Berets were inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Were those Chetniks that had been in Buna, were they also there, or just the Red Berets?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: There were only members of the Red Berets there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What was the camp used for by them? What was done in the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: The camp was used as a basis for the Red Berets, and they conducted training there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Who was trained there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: As I said, I myself and another young man was collected up in Nevesinje with Pero Divljak and Aco, and we came to the Boracka Jezero camp, and they were all there. But they weren't actually men. They were very young, children almost, and they were all rounded up from the village of Borci, which is across from the lake, the Boracko Lake.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean they trained new recruits?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: How many Red Berets were there to train these young people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: I have told you of all those that I could think of, 10 or 12 of them. I can't be quite specific. Generally speaking, it was the group that arrived at the Buna.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So those you mean you listed in tab 2, all these people you listed in tab 2, the chart with all the names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes, that's who I'm thinking of. Not all of them, because some of them had left. Actually, just one left. All the others were still there, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: The training the young men received there consisted of what? What -- just briefly, what kind of training did you get?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Well, it was the same sort of training that those men had attended, or as far as I could see, that they went through in Knin with Captain Dragan, the same drills. And this was done under their supervision and it was their military training, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And how do you know that it was the same training? Were any -- any training materials used from Knin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what kind of material was used, but I saw the tapes that they showed us, which were taken in Knin, the footage of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see a person, Major Fico, on these tapes? And if so, what did you see him do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes, I did see that individual, and they said his name was Major Fico. And he was conducting a training exercise using a knife.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did Frenki visit -- Frenki Simatovic visit the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you describe what happened, how he arrived and what happened.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: First they had said that the camp had to be cleaned up and put in order, and then they placed some benches in the headquarters. Frenki arrived by helicopter. We were all lined up. Aco Legija reported to him about the situation in the camp. I can't remember everything he said, but he said how many men there were in the camp and the level of readiness in the camp and military, things of that kind. Then Frenki delivered a patriotic speech about the Serbian knights and the successes scored by the Red Berets. I can't remember the exact wording of the speech. But there was this patriotic schund being delivered. And once that was over, the speech of his, we went into a room that they used as headquarters where we were given according to CZ-99 the pistols that had arrived with Frenki, and we were told that we would have to write the CVs of all of us in order to become members of the Red Berets, to write a curriculum vitae for membership.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Was that the first time that you saw Frenki Simatovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes, that was my -- the first and last time I ever saw him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did he introduce himself or was he introduced by his name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: No. After Aco Legija reported to him, he gave us his full name and surname and then proceeded to deliver his speech.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And you have mentioned a pistol that arrived with Frenki Simatovic. Did you get that pistol?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Was that a present, or what was the occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: What it was exactly, I don't know. You'll have to ask Frenki that. But all the new arrivals were given a pistol, because all the old ones, the Red Berets, already had these CZ-99-type pistols.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Private session, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In the vicinity of the Red Beret camp, was there also an army facility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes. Across from the river was the village of Borci, and the members of the Serb forces were put up there. They had their facilities. This was when the Serb forces were transformed into the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And did these Serb forces cooperate with the Red Berets and the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: While you were in the camp, did you observe any atrocities or any indications of atrocities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: On one occasion, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What did you see? What happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: It was night-time, and I was coming back from the village of Borci, and at the entrance to the camp, once I had entered the camp - and you can see that on the diagram here - as you enter the camp, on the left-hand side there is the command facility and there was a man in civilian clothes standing there with his hands tied behind his back. Two or three minutes later or one minute later Pero Divljak picked the man up and took him off in the direction of the lake. He didn't see me or the guard I was with. However, Pero came back very quickly after that and his knife was all bloody, covered in blood, and he began screaming at me, what was I doing there, why wasn't I in bed, it was high time I was in bed, and he kicked me and I left.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see any women in the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: During the night, yes -- no, actually, during the next day, because during the night a state of emergency had been proclaimed, and so where I was lying -- actually, there's a light in front of each bungalow, and I was able to see that the members of the Red Berets were coming and going. There was a lot of coming and going amongst the Red Berets throughout that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And you -- when did you see the women?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: It was either the following day or two days later.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Where were the women? Where in the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: As I've already said in my statement, I wasn't actually in the camp when they brought them in. That's why I didn't see them straight away. However, the women were in the bungalow, from which the Red Berets were coming and going throughout the night, going in and coming out. And I saw them either the next day or two days after from a distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you learn what ethnicity these women had and what happened to them while in the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes. And not only me, but all the others too. We learnt what had happened the following day, because the next day the local Serbs from Zaborani turned up and we learnt from them that they were Muslims from Fazlagic Kula.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And do you know whether these women were assaulted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: I can't say anything about that. I can just tell you what I saw. I did see the Red Berets going into their bungalow and out of it throughout the night. Now, what actually happened, I can't say. I didn't see it myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Let's briefly speak about a few other camps, Red Beret camps. Were you aware that the Red Berets had a camp in Fruska Gora? And if so, who was in charge there and what else did you learn about it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: I did learn that the Red Berets had not only a camp at Fruska Gora but several camps, in fact. And most of those stories, most of that information I learned from Pero Divljak. Although, I learned about it from others as well. And what I heard from them was the man who could collect up anybody he wished from any camps was called Zivojin Ivanovic, nicknamed Zika Crnogorac, the Montenegrin.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever meet this person, and how could he pick up each person he wanted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Ah, well, yes. I got to know this bestial person in human form. He was indeed the commander of the camps. And not only from Pero Divljak, but I heard about -- stories going round about the power of Zika Crnogorac, the power he wielded. utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did Pero Divljak tell you about a visit of Frenki in Fruska Gora camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Pero Divljak told me that they - I don't know where they came from - or rather, they had returned from Croatia or somewhere else to Lezimir at Fruska Gora, and they were in the camp for about 20 days without any television sets, radios, just training. And after 20 days of this, Frenki turned up and they were all lined up and told that there were demonstrations going on in Belgrade and that they were a unit belonging to the system and anybody who wanted to do any shooting could leave. Pay Divljak tried to leave but he was saved by Ilija Vuckovic, Rambo, who took him by the hand and said that this was just a joke, which turned out to be true, because all those who did step down were actually taken to the hangar by this same man Zika Crnogorac, where they were well beaten up.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Were you aware that there was a Tara camp in Mitrovac in Montenegro? And if so, who was in charge of this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: Yes, I was aware of that. I did hear of the Tara camp and that Zika Crnogorac was in charge of that camp too. The man who told me this in actual fact was one of his instructors, and his name was Duco Durutovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And one last question: Were you told where the Red Berets from the Tara camp had actions, where did they get involved?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017
utterances.text: What I can tell you about that is this: I saw a document once which indicated that the Red Berets were operational around the area of Zeleni Jadar, or rather, the mine of Osmaci and the area of Srebrenica, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, that's obviously convenient. We'll adjourn now until tomorrow morning, 9.00. Could you be back, Witness C-017, then, at 9.00 tomorrow morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
